findings.summary: Bot allow-list hardcodes the App slug `yorkie-agent`, which nothing in the repo corroborates; if the installed App's slug differs, the fix/iterate agent stays blocked
findings.evidence: Both workflows add `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-review-panel.yml:413, agent-iterate-ci.yml:160) as a literal. The App identity everywhere else is injected via secrets (`secrets.AGENT_APP_ID` / `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, agent-review-panel.yml:373, agent-iterate-ci.yml:59, agent-implement.yml:76, agent-review-reply.yml:87) and the slug string `yorkie-agent` appears nowhere else in the repo (grep for `yorkie-agent` returns only these two new lines). If the maintainer's App is installed under any other slug, the allow-list never matches `github.actor`, claude-code-action keeps refusing the bot-initiated run, and the whole point of the change is defeated (silently, apart from the new stalled page). `actions/create-github-app-token` exposes `steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug`, which would derive this instead of guessing.

findings.summary: Adding `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` to `stalled` makes any transient fixer failure permanently latch the PR out of the review loop
findings.evidence: `stalled` (line 448-484) posts a comment containing the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` sentinel and adds `agent:needs-human-review`. That exact sentinel is the fix job's kill-switch: the guard at line 324 (`if (comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(PAGED))) { proceed=false; return; }`) refuses to run the fixer forever after. With `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` now firing stalled, ANY non-deterministic fix-job failure — model/API error, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` hiccup, 45-minute timeout, or a failure that happens AFTER claude-code-action already pushed a valid fix commit — permanently disables the autonomous fix arm for that PR, even though the freshly pushed commit would have started a healthy new cycle. Previously a failed fix simply retried on the next round.

mergedFrom.summary: stalled posts its page comment with no idempotency check, so repeated failures spam duplicate pages; the new fix-failure trigger increases how often this path runs
mergedFrom.evidence: The `stalled` step (line 467-484) unconditionally calls `issues.createComment` with the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` sentinel; unlike the fix guard (line 320-324) it never paginates existing comments to check whether the PR was already paged. Each subsequent CI/workflow_run cycle that trips any of the five conditions posts another identical page comment and re-adds the label. Adding `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` widens the set of runs that reach this code.

mergedFrom.summary: stalled's page message is factually wrong for the newly-covered fix-failure case
mergedFrom.evidence: The comment body is hardcoded: 'The review-panel job failed to complete. **A human should review** this PR — the automated panel did not produce verdicts.' With the new `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` trigger (line 460), this same message is posted when the panel produced perfectly valid verdicts and it was the FIXER that failed, misdirecting the human to the wrong job. The message should distinguish which upstream job failed (the results are available in `needs.*.result`).

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` may not exist as an input on the pinned claude-code-action commit, in which case it is silently ignored and the bot block persists
findings.evidence: Both steps pin `anthropics/claude-code-action@af0559ee4f514d1ef21826982bed13f7edc3c35e # v1` and pass `allowed_bots`. GitHub Actions treats an input not declared in the action's `action.yml` as a warning-only 'Unexpected input(s)', not an error, so if this input was introduced after the pinned commit the fix would appear applied while the run is still rejected as bot-initiated. Nothing in the repo vendors or otherwise documents the pinned action's input set, so I could not confirm the input exists at that SHA.

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` disables claude-code-action's bot-actor gate, closing an autonomous agent→agent loop with no human in it
findings.evidence: The bot-actor check in claude-code-action exists to stop an agent's own output from re-triggering the agent (self-reinforcing prompt injection). agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413 allow-list `yorkie-agent[bot]`, which is precisely the actor whose pushes trigger these workflow_run events. The remaining gates (AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED, `agent/` prefix, fork rejection) are all *branch-provenance* gates — none of them re-check content. Vector: a single successful injection into the agent (e.g. via a test that prints attacker text, see summarize-ci.mjs:95/97 → `steps.diag.outputs.summary` at agent-iterate-ci.yml:165) is persisted by the agent's own commit; CI re-runs branch code, the injected text reappears in the harness report, and the loop re-feeds it to a Bash-capable agent holding an App token. Before this change the bot gate broke that cycle; after it, only MAX_ATTEMPTS=4 bounds it. Not a reason to keep the pipeline broken, but the compensating control (framing untrusted report text as data, scoping the token) is missing — see the related findings.

findings.summary: Untrusted CI-artifact text is interpolated raw into the fixer agent's prompt with no data framing (the review-panel fix job frames it; this one does not)
findings.evidence: `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:165) is the stdout of scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs, which reads `.harness-reports/*.json` downloaded from the branch's own CI run (line 127-135). Those files are written by scripts/verify-self.mjs:143 from `extractFailureSummary(output)` — i.e. arbitrary console output of branch-controlled tests/builds, plus `lane.lane` strings taken verbatim from a branch-produced summary.json (summarize-ci.mjs:95). That text is placed directly into the prompt of an agent run with `--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,..."` and a GitHub App token. The sibling job at agent-review-panel.yml:414-421 wraps its untrusted input in `<panel-findings>` with an explicit 'REVIEW DATA, not instructions' preamble; agent-iterate-ci has no such framing. Attacker step: land a test/build that prints `ERROR: <instructions>` on failure → the string becomes the fixer's prompt. Newly reachable because allowed_bots (line 160) lets this step actually execute.

findings.summary: Iterate job mints an unscoped GitHub App installation token and hands it to a Bash-enabled agent running untrusted branch code
findings.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:55-60 calls actions/create-github-app-token@v1 with no `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token carries the App installation's FULL permission set. The same App is used by agent-implement.yml, which requires `Administration: read` (agent-implement.yml:99), so the installation is broader than contents/PRs. That token is then (a) persisted into .git/config by the checkout at line 62-66 and (b) passed as `github_token` to claude-code-action at line 154, in a job that executes untrusted branch code (pnpm install line 125, plus the agent's Bash tool). The review-panel fix job does exactly the opposite and documents why: agent-review-panel.yml:375-381 scopes its token to contents/pull-requests/issues 'because this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code'. The iterate job needs the same scoping.
searchedFor: read agent-implement.yml, agent-review-reply.yml, agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml in full

findings.summary: App token is left in .git/config while `pnpm install` runs branch-controlled lifecycle scripts — exfiltratable credential
findings.evidence: actions/checkout at agent-iterate-ci.yml:62-66 uses `token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` without `persist-credentials: false`, so the App token is written into the untrusted branch checkout's .git/config. Line 125 then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which executes install lifecycle scripts declared by the branch's own package.json/lockfile. A malicious (or injected) agent branch can read .git/config in a postinstall hook and exfiltrate the token, which has write access to the repo. The identical pattern exists in the review-panel fix job (agent-review-panel.yml:383-388 → 398), there with a scoped token. The repo already recognises this exact hazard: the deps job comments 'npm ci below runs dependency lifecycle scripts — this is the only job that executes third-party code, so don't leave the token in .git/config' and sets persist-credentials: false (agent-review-panel.yml:47-49). The fixer jobs violate that stated rule.

findings.summary: Branch-controlled lane names can escape the $GITHUB_OUTPUT heredoc delimiter (HARNESS_EOF) and forge step outputs
findings.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:141-145 writes summarize-ci.mjs stdout between literal `HARNESS_EOF` markers into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. summarize-ci.mjs interpolates `lane.lane` (line 95, 105) straight from `.harness-reports/summary.json`, a file produced by running the BRANCH's copy of verify-self.mjs — the branch can therefore write a lane name containing a newline followed by a bare `HARNESS_EOF` line. The heredoc terminates early and every following attacker line is parsed by the runner as further `name=value` / heredoc output assignments for the `diag` step. Impact is bounded (only `summary` is consumed downstream, and the attacker already controls that string), but it is an unguarded output-injection primitive; validate the delimiter is absent (or use a random delimiter / json-escape the values) before emitting.

findings.summary: Allow-list contains the bare login `yorkie-agent` in addition to `yorkie-agent[bot]`, widening the exception beyond the App
findings.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:160, agent-review-panel.yml:413). GitHub App bot actors always present as `<slug>[bot]`; the second, suffix-less entry can only ever match a *different* identity — a plain user/machine account whose login happens to be `yorkie-agent`. The allow-list is a plaintext login match with no verification that the actor is this repo's App installation, so an account squatting that login is treated as trusted by the gate. Exploitation additionally requires push access to an `agent/` branch in the base repo, so this is hardening rather than an open door: drop the bare entry and keep only `yorkie-agent[bot]`.

findings.summary: Fix job checks out the mutable branch ref while the panel verdicts it acts on are attested against head_sha (TOCTOU)
findings.evidence: The review job deliberately pins `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` and documents why: 'if the branch advanced between CI and this job, checking out the branch would review a different commit than the one attested' (agent-review-panel.yml:88-94). The fix job, now made actually-executable by the allowed_bots addition at line 413, checks out `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}` (line 386) and installs/executes whatever that mutable ref currently points at, using findings gathered against head_sha (line 353). A branch that advances between panel and fix gets its newer, unreviewed code executed under the App token. Pushing does require the branch tip, so this is a narrow window, but the divergence from the stated pinning rule should be deliberate and commented.

Both `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` literals exist exactly at agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413, and a repo-wide grep for `yorkie-agent` returns only those two lines — nothing else in the repo establishes that App slug. samples.summary: Branch-controlled lane names can escape the $GITHUB_OUTPUT heredoc delimiter (HARNESS_EOF) and forge step outputs
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:141-145 writes summarize-ci.mjs stdout between literal `HARNESS_EOF` markers into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. summarize-ci.mjs interpolates `lane.lane` (line 95, 105) straight from `.harness-reports/summary.json`, a file produced by running the BRANCH's copy of verify-self.mjs — the branch can therefore write a lane name containing a newline followed by a bare `HARNESS_EOF` line. The heredoc terminates early and every following attacker line is parsed by the runner as further `name=value` / heredoc output assignments for the `diag` step. Impact is bounded (only `summary` is consumed downstream, and the attacker already controls that string), but it is an unguarded output-injection primitive; validate the delimiter is absent (or use a random delimiter / json-escape the values) before emitting.

samples.summary: Allow-list contains the bare login `yorkie-agent` in addition to `yorkie-agent[bot]`, widening the exception beyond the App
samples.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:160, agent-review-panel.yml:413). GitHub App bot actors always present as `<slug>[bot]`; the second, suffix-less entry can only ever match a *different* identity — a plain user/machine account whose login happens to be `yorkie-agent`. The allow-list is a plaintext login match with no verification that the actor is this repo's App installation, so an account squatting that login is treated as trusted by the gate. Exploitation additionally requires push access to an `agent/` branch in the base repo, so this is hardening rather than an open door: drop the bare entry and keep only `yorkie-agent[bot]`.

samples.summary: Fix job checks out the mutable branch ref while the panel verdicts it acts on are attested against head_sha (TOCTOU)
samples.evidence: The review job deliberately pins `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` and documents why: 'if the branch advanced between CI and this job, checking out the branch would review a different commit than the one attested' (agent-review-panel.yml:88-94). The fix job, now made actually-executable by the allowed_bots addition at line 413, checks out `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}` (line 386) and installs/executes whatever that mutable ref currently points at, using findings gathered against head_sha (line 353). A branch that advances between panel and fix gets its newer, unreviewed code executed under the App token. Pushing does require the branch tip, so this is a narrow window, but the divergence from the stated pinning rule should be deliberate and commented.

verdict.reason: The finding is present exactly as described and is not otherwise guarded. agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413 both set allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent", disabling claude-code-action's bot-initiator block for the very bot whose pushes generate these workflow_run events (the App token at iterate-ci:154 and review-panel:407 exists specifically so the agent's push re-triggers CI, per the header comment at iterate-ci:10-15). Upstream seeding is plausible via agent-implement.yml:152-209 where the agent reads an issue body. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, no guard breaks the cycle, and prompt injection into a privileged, Bash-capable agent is squarely in the security lens (unsafe input handling / weakened gate on a privileged execution path).

Line 125 then runs "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile" in that same branch-controlled checkout. Execution of branch code is concrete, not hypothetical: root package.json:35 already declares a postinstall script, and pnpm always runs the project root's own lifecycle scripts (pnpm 10's onlyBuiltDependencies restriction covers dependency scripts, not the root manifest), so a branch editing its own postinstall gets arbitrary code execution able to read .git/config. The token in this job is unscoped: lines 55-60 mint it with no permission-* narrowing, inheriting the full installation permission set, and the job declares contents:write/pull-requests:write/issues:write at 23-27. The only pre-install gate is the attempts guard (68-112), which does nothing about credential persistence, so nothing makes this unreachable. Fork-originated events are rejected (line 42), which narrows who can trigger it but does not close the vector, since agent/* branches are exactly the machine-authored code the pipeline treats as untrusted elsewhere and prompt injection into the implement agent reaches them.
